internal.title: Incident Report: Checkout Service High Error Rate Due to Payment Service Failure
internal.body:
At 12:03 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service. Initial diagnosis identified a 100% error rate in the payment service, indicating it as the root cause. The checkout service also showed elevated errors and latency, and the frontend service had increased errors, but these were secondary effects.

The mitigation involved disabling the paymentFailure flag at 12:23 UTC after approval, which immediately resolved the issue. Error rates returned to normal levels shortly after.

Key timeline:
- 12:03:28: Alert received for checkout service error rate
- 12:23:09: Diagnosis confirmed payment service error injection
- 12:23:15: Payment failure flag disabled after approval
- 12:23:15: Recovery verified with error rates normalized

This incident highlights the critical dependency of checkout on payment service stability and the importance of rapid flag management for mitigation.

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment service issues
external.body: Between 12:03 and 12:23 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced failures completing checkout due to issues in the payment processing service. The issue was identified and resolved within 20 minutes, restoring normal service operation. We apologize for any inconvenience caused and are working to prevent similar issues in the future.

lessons.lesson: Ensure multi-approver workflows for critical flag changes are streamlined to minimize mitigation delay during incidents.

action_items: Review and improve alerting thresholds for payment service errors to detect issues earlier.
Conduct a post-incident review with the payment and checkout teams to identify preventive measures.
Evaluate the flag approval process to reduce time to mitigation during incidents.
